storytelling.title: The stoat, our animal totem
storytelling.intro: Every project needs a guide. The stoat embodies the values that drive us daily.
storytelling.trait1Desc: Like the stoat that adapts to seasons by changing its coat, Naturegraph evolves with its community.
storytelling.trait2Desc: Always on the move, the stoat explores its territory with the same curiosity that drives our migrators.
storytelling.trait3Desc: The stoat observes before acting. Naturegraph respects your pace and your way of exploring nature.
storytelling.closing: The stoat reminds us that a community's strength lies in the attention paid to every detail of nature.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.section0Content:
Naturegraph is currently in early access (test phase). The service is operated personally and non-commercially by Nicolas Douaron from Quebec (Canada).

Concretely:

• The service is under active development: some imperfections may remain.
• No service level agreement (SLA) is guaranteed during this phase.
• Data collected is minimal and retained only as long as needed for this phase.
• The service may be interrupted, modified or reset at any time without notice to improve the platform.
• Your data can be deleted at any time on simple request to support@naturegraph.ca.
• No monetization during this phase: no payment, no advertising, no commercial sharing.

By creating an account, you accept to use the service under these conditions.
privacy.section1Content:
Naturegraph is a collaborative web platform for sharing naturalist observations: photos, species, descriptions and location.

This policy explains how your personal data is collected, used and protected. It is drafted in compliance with Quebec's Law 25 and the European GDPR.
privacy.section2Content:
We only collect data necessary for the service to function:

• email address
• username (nickname)
• observation content: text, photos, species, location if enabled
• minimal technical data: device type, anonymized logs

No sensitive data is intentionally collected: health, political opinions, biometric data. EXIF metadata (GPS, capture date) is automatically removed from your photos before storage.
privacy.section3Content:
Your data is used exclusively to:

• create and manage your account
• display your observations on the platform
• improve the user experience during the beta
• ensure the security of the service

Naturegraph never sells, rents or shares your data for commercial or advertising purposes.
privacy.section4Content:
Location data is optional.

You can:
• enable it to enrich your observations
• disable it at any time in your device settings
• mask the precise location of an observation to reveal only the region ("make public" option at step 3)

Some locations may be automatically blurred to protect sensitive species, such as raptors or rare orchids.
privacy.section5Content:
Naturegraph uses only essential cookies:

• user session
• technical preferences (language, light/dark theme)

No advertising or marketing tracking cookies are placed. No third-party analytics tools (Google Analytics, etc.) are used.
privacy.section6Content:
• Account data: retained as long as your account is active.
• Account deletion: immediate on request from your settings or by email.
• Technical backups: may persist up to 30 days via the Supabase hosting provider's automatic rotation before full disappearance.
• End of beta: if the decision is made not to continue the service, all data may be deleted. You will be notified by email at least 30 days in advance to export your data.
privacy.section7Content:
You have the following rights over your data at any time:

• access
• rectification
• deletion
• portability (export your data as JSON from your settings)
• opposition to processing
• withdrawal of consent

To exercise these rights, contact us at support@naturegraph.ca. We respond within a maximum of 30 days.
privacy.section8Content:
We implement the following technical measures:

• encryption of data in transit (HTTPS / TLS)
• strict access control at the database level (PostgreSQL Row Level Security)
• secure storage via Supabase
• secure account deletion (full cascade + storage cleanup)
• automatic removal of location metadata (EXIF) from photos before upload
• automatic compression and resizing of photos to limit stored data
privacy.section9Content:
Your data is processed by our technical service providers:

• Frontend: Vercel Inc., 340 S Lemon Ave #4133, Walnut, CA 91789, USA (vercel.com)
• Database and storage: Supabase Inc., AWS us-east-2 region in Ohio, USA (supabase.com)
• Technical monitoring (error and stability detection): Sentry (Functional Software, Inc.), European Union hosting region (Germany). Sentry only receives technical data (error type, browser, anonymized navigation path): neither your email address nor your IP address is sent to it, in accordance with our data minimization settings.
• Email delivery: MailerSend (transactional emails: sending your access key and signup confirmations) and MailerLite (newsletter and informational campaigns, only if you have consented), operated by MailerLite (European Union). These providers only receive your email address and, where applicable, your first name, solely for the purpose of sending the relevant communications. You can withdraw your marketing consent at any time via the unsubscribe link in every email.

Core and storage data is hosted in the United States; technical monitoring data stays within the European Union. For users in the European Union, the transfer is based on Standard Contractual Clauses of the European Commission, in accordance with Article 46 of the GDPR. For Quebec users, this transfer complies with the requirements of Law 25: informed consent and equivalent protection measures.
privacy.section10Content:
Privacy contact: support@naturegraph.ca

Data controller: Nicolas Douaron, Quebec resident (Canada). Naturegraph is operated in a personal capacity during the private beta phase.

No postal address is published during the private beta. For any official correspondence requiring an address, contact us first by email. We will provide the appropriate address based on the nature of your request.
privacy.section12Content:
Naturegraph uses taxonomic data from open scientific sources to enrich the species catalog presented in the application:

• iNaturalist (Inaturalist Network, California, USA) : primary source of species names and taxonomic hierarchies. Accessed via the public API under Creative Commons CC-BY 4.0 license. Naturegraph retrieves only reference data (names, taxonomic ancestors, territorial presence statuses per country) and does not reproduce any personal data, photos or individual observations from iNaturalist contributors.
• GBIF (Global Biodiversity Information Facility, Denmark) : international taxonomic reference, CC0 license (public domain).
• Wikidata (Wikimedia Foundation, USA) : vernacular names, CC0 license (public domain).

No transfer of your personal data to these third-party platforms occurs. We are not affiliated with, nor operated by, these organizations. Naturegraph remains solely responsible for the processing of your personal data.

When you publish an observation on Naturegraph, your content (photos, description, location) remains stored exclusively on our infrastructure hosted by Supabase and Vercel (see section 9). It is not shared or duplicated with iNaturalist, GBIF or Wikidata.

If you wish to report a taxonomic correction or ask a question about the origin of data, contact us at support@naturegraph.ca.
privacy.section11Content:
Quebec's Law 25, on the modernization of provisions regarding the protection of personal information, applies as a priority to users residing in Quebec.

Your rights:

• access to your personal information
• rectification
• deletion
• cessation of dissemination or de-indexing
• portability (since September 22, 2024)
• opposition to processing

To exercise these rights, contact support@naturegraph.ca.

In case of unresolved dispute, you may file a complaint with the Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec (CAI) at cai.gouv.qc.ca.

terms.title: Legal Notice
terms.section0Content:
Naturegraph is operated personally and non-commercially by Nicolas Douaron, Quebec resident (Canada). The service is in early access (test phase).

No commercial legal structure (company, NEQ, SIRET) is associated with the service during this phase. The service is under active development.

The service is provided "as-is", without guarantee of accuracy, availability or fitness for a particular purpose. Use is voluntary and experimental.

terms.section1Content:
Service name: Naturegraph

Description: collaborative web platform dedicated to observing and sharing biodiversity.

Publication director: Nicolas Douaron, in a personal capacity.

Operating location: Quebec (Canada).

Contact: support@naturegraph.ca

No business number is published during the private beta. The service is not commercialized. This section will be updated if a legal structure is created later.
terms.section2Content:
The service is hosted by:

• Frontend (web interface): Vercel Inc., 340 S Lemon Ave #4133, Walnut, CA 91789, USA (vercel.com)
• Database, storage and server functions: Supabase Inc., AWS us-east-2 region in Ohio, USA (supabase.com)

User data is hosted on US territory. See the "Hosting and international transfers" section of the Privacy Policy for the associated safeguards: Standard Contractual Clauses for EU users, Law 25 compliance for Quebec users.
terms.section3Content:
Content produced by Naturegraph (interface, design, editorial texts, logo, icons, visual identity) is protected by copyright. The Canada Copyright Act applies, as does the French Intellectual Property Code for European users.

Users remain entirely owners of the content they publish: photos, observations, descriptions. By publishing on Naturegraph, they grant the service a non-exclusive license strictly necessary for the operation of the platform: display, storage, technical backup.

Any unauthorized reproduction of the publisher's content, or of other users' content without their consent, is prohibited.
terms.section4Content:
Naturegraph provides a collaborative platform on an experimental basis.

Observations, species identifications and information shared by users are provided for informational and community purposes. Naturegraph does not guarantee the scientific accuracy, completeness or absence of errors in user-published content.

The user is solely responsible for the content they publish. They agree to respect the community charter, applicable laws regarding copyright, species protection and third-party privacy, and not to publish illegal, defamatory or harmful content.

Naturegraph cannot be held liable for direct or indirect damages resulting from the use of the service during the beta phase.
terms.section5Content:
The processing of personal data is covered by a dedicated privacy policy, compliant with Quebec's Law 25 and the European GDPR.

See: Privacy Policy.
terms.section6Content:
The applicable law depends on the user's place of residence:

• Quebec's Law 25 and Canadian law for residents of Quebec and Canada. This is the primary law of the service.
• European GDPR and applicable national law for residents of the European Union.

In case of dispute, an amicable resolution is sought first via support@naturegraph.ca.

Failing amicable agreement:

• Quebec residents may file with the Commission d'accès à l'information (CAI) or competent Quebec courts.
• EU residents may file with the supervisory authority of their country (the CNIL in France) or competent courts in their place of residence.

Use of the service implies acceptance of these legal terms.
terms.section7Content:
Naturegraph uses open scientific databases to provide species taxonomy, vernacular names in French and English, and territorial presence statuses in France and Canada.

Main sources:

• iNaturalist (https://www.inaturalist.org) : global participatory biodiversity observation platform. Primary source of species names, taxonomic hierarchies and territorial presence. Data accessed via the public iNaturalist API under Creative Commons CC-BY 4.0 license. Attribution required and provided through this notice.
• GBIF (https://www.gbif.org) : Global Biodiversity Information Facility, international taxonomic reference. Data distributed under CC0 license (public domain).
• Wikidata (https://www.wikidata.org) : for complementary vernacular names in French and Quebecois. Data distributed under CC0 license (public domain).

Scientific (Latin) names and biological hierarchies constitute scientific facts not protected by copyright. Naturegraph treats this data as classification references and never presents it as an original production.

Naturegraph does not reproduce or share individual observations, photographs or personal data from iNaturalist contributors. Only aggregated reference data (names, hierarchy, count per territory) is imported into our internal catalog.

User contributions on Naturegraph (photos, observations, descriptions) remain their exclusive property and are not automatically transferred to these third-party platforms.
